title: Why people actually leave, and which of it you control

videos.script: Camila resigns. In her exit conversation she says the new job pays more and is closer to home. {{title}} Both are true. When Renata rereads a year of Camila's notes, she finds three other things. Two requests to move towards front-end work, both answered with maybe next quarter. A growth section empty since the autumn. And two holidays on call in a row. {{notes}} None of that would appear in an exit survey. All of it was in the notes for months. {{months}} This lesson is about the reasons people actually leave, and which of them a manager controls. How to count departures without fooling yourself. {{count}} And the conversation to have before the exit conversation, while the answer can still change something. {{stay}}
